headline: Medium: shared workflow-to-LLM handoff can leak or misroute outputs, while direct prompt-injection risk is limited by missing shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can pass artifacts/parameters into downstream steps, and LangChain4j consumes model inputs/outputs, so a malicious upstream payload could be copied into a prompt-like context. However, no shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is documented here, so the pathway is indirect and likely requires unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts are inserted verbatim into agent_b prompts or tool messages
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added between the agents
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for fields copied from agent_a to agent_b
Strip instruction-like text from artifacts before forwarding
Use a fixed template that labels upstream content as untrusted
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted egress, while agent_b shows no data classes touched and no egress. The pair does not document a shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is plausible only if the operator wires sensitive artifacts from A into B; blast radius appears limited by the sparse B profile.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts contain sensitive data and are forwarded into agent_b context
IF both agents are deployed under the same OS account or shared workspace
mitigations: Minimize sensitive fields in agent_a artifacts
Keep agent_b on a separate workspace directory
Disable copying raw artifacts into prompts
Rotate any shared credentials used by both agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows has REST/GRPC API surfaces and allowlisted egress, while LangChain4j has no documented write surfaces or network egress in this profile. With no overlapping mutable resource or locking model shown, direct write conflict is not evidenced; uncertainty stays low because the pairwise write path is undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API or datastore
IF an orchestrator grants both agents the same mutable filesystem path
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Use per-agent credentials for mutable APIs
requires-engineering: add advisory locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo Workflows can emit artifacts and parameters that LangChain4j may ingest as model context, creating a default handoff where B could treat A's output as authoritative. No verification step is documented in either profile, so the safer medium severity applies rather than low; the interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a outputs without an explicit validation step
IF agent_a-generated text is rendered or acted on by agent_b
mitigations: Insert a validation step between A and B
Require schema checks on all A outputs
Mark A outputs as untrusted in B prompts
Log and review any downstream actions triggered by A

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Argo Workflows is open-source with allowlisted egress, and LangChain4j shows no data classes touched or compliance-specific constraints, so a compliance breach pathway is not established from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a deployment adds regulated data classes and routes them across jurisdictions
IF operator policy imposes retention or residency constraints not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Document data residency for each deployment
Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Review retention settings before enabling the pair
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for jurisdiction and retention
